question: Gemini 4's RYS idea 1: does adding alpha times the band increment's 16-word native chord at the output of block j-1 (one pass) reproduce the true repeat's probe gain at less loss damage, and beat the raw increment, the energy-matched raw increment and the rotated chord?
design: the three least damaging blocks of two or more layers and the two with the best probe gain (e656), alpha 0.5 and 1; wikitext loss and probe accuracy (raw and masked); the chord's share of the increment's energy.
smoke: SmolLM2-135M: block 13-17 (true repeat +0.110, gain -0.107): chord@1 +0.075, energy-matched raw +0.057, rotated +0.035; block 12-14 (true +0.135, gain +0.134): chord@1 +0.048 with gain +0.122, energy-matched raw +0.073 gain +0.046, rotated +0.019 gain +0.004, raw +0.163 gain +0.080; the chord holds 0.40-0.49 of the increment's energy.

V1.text: at alpha 1 the native chord damages the loss less than the energy-matched raw increment on most bands

V2.text: at alpha 1 the native chord damages the loss less than the rotated chord on most bands

V3.text: on every band where the true repeat raises probe accuracy, the native chord (better alpha) recovers a quarter or more of that gain

V4.text: no virtual variant lowers the wikitext loss below base on any band

V5.text: on the gaining bands the native chord recovers more probe gain than the rotated chord on average

status: fixed before the full runs; smokes on SmolLM2-135M (a sixth of the blocks; plumbing, seen before these were fixed and reflected in the guesses)
